newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's Aasgard licensees sign Statpipe deal.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Aasgard licensees sign Statpipe deal.

text.p: The licensees of the Aasgard development off mid-Norway have signed a processing agreement with the Statpipe partners covering 200 billion cubic metres of gas, Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday.
The agreeement, which took 18 months to finalise, runs from October 1, 2000 to 2027.

A deal also was reached on tying the Aasgard Transport gas pipeline, running from the Aasgard field to the Kaarstoe terminal north of Stavanger, into the Statpipe trunkline, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
The processing agreement will double capacity at the Kaarstoe treatment plant and will require new investment of between four and 4.2 billion crowns.
Following the Aasgard Transport deal, pipelines with an overall capacity annual capacity of 28 billion cubic metres will be tied into Kaarstoe.
"With the processing agreement and the big investment at Kaarstoe, the basis is also laid for further gas sales from the Halten Bank area off mid-Norway," Statoil said.
The Aasgard licensees are operator Statoil, Agip, Saga Petroleum, Neste, Mobil, Total and Norsk Hydro.
The Statpipe partners are Statoil, Elf, Norsk Hydro, Esso, Mobil, Shell, Total, Conoco and Saga.
